description: Shared correctness fixtures (docs/benchmark-correctness-fixtures.md). Every dataset processes the identical logical range [0, totalIterations) via sum(i), partitioned differently by worker count: numericLoop and nativeSleepDowncall use ONE worker summing the whole range; threadFleet splits it evenly across fleetSize workers. Because integer summation is partition-invariant, all three datasets produce the IDENTICAL total — worker count and native-call interleaving change TTSP/pause behavior, never the computed result. Variant-specific extras (idle threads, an additional native-blocked thread, organic-vs-explicit GC triggering, the -XX:-UseCountedLoopSafepoints launch flag) never contribute to the checksum.

semantics.operation: sum(i) for i in [0, totalIterations), 64-bit wrapping
semantics.numericLoop: one worker sums the full range in 8 chunks of 50,000,000, calling an explicit safepoint trigger between chunks
semantics.nativeSleepDowncall: one worker, identical chunking, PLUS one usleep(50000) FFM downcall between each chunk
semantics.threadFleet: 16 workers, each summing a disjoint 25,000,000-element sub-range; only worker 0 chunks (8x) and triggers safepoints, the other 15 run their sub-range as one continuous pass
semantics.cooperativeLoop: default JVM safepoint-poll behavior (no special flags) — the control
semantics.threadInNativeCall: adds one extra thread blocked in a long usleep FFM downcall for the duration of the run
semantics.manyIdleThreads: adds idleThreadCount extra threads parked in Thread.sleep for the duration of the run
semantics.allocationPressureTrigger: the trigger worker allocates a garbage array every chunk instead of calling an explicit safepoint trigger — GC-induced safepoints occur organically; the exact count is host/heap-dependent by design, unlike every other variant's exactly numChunks-triggered count
